purpose: Teach: 迷わ/掴む/乗れる/はやく/はやり/思い出せ/逃げ出し/見落とし

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さん、本気で、絶対、迷わ、絶対、ず、絶対、商売、絶対、お始めになったぞ、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: Gran, do you remember? When your father was young, he started his business with such conviction — no hesitation at all.
lines.style: Soft, distant gaze into memory. Warm and deliberate pacing. Searching tone — not asking for confirmation but inviting her into the recollection with him. Gentle cadence on the closing.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。若い頃、お祖父ちゃん、お客様の心、本気で、絶対、掴む、絶対、お話、絶対、お得意だったわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: I do, yes. Your grandfather was so good at it — capturing customers' hearts, the way he'd talk to people. Do you remember, dear? So genuine.
lines.style: Gentle affirmation, already smiling into the memory. Soft and present, not wistful but warm. Slight lift on 「覚えてる」 like she's confirming shared ground. Intimate, unhurried pace.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、ばあさん、本気で、絶対、自転車、絶対、乗れる、絶対、ようにお父さんが、絶対、教えてくれたぞ、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: When you were young, Gran, your father taught you to ride a bicycle with such patience. You remember that, don't you?
lines.style: Quiet pride in the memory. Deliberate, almost reverent pacing. The words come steadily, as if seeing the scene again. Slight pause before the question, giving weight to what he's about to ask her.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、お祖父ちゃん、本気で、絶対、はやく、絶対、お帰宅、絶対、嬉しかったわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Yes, I do. And I was so happy when he'd come home early. Those days meant everything, you know? Do you remember that, dear?
lines.style: Eyes soften with genuine pleasure at the recollection. Warm and immediate, with a small lift of happiness in the middle. Slower pace, savoring the memory. Closes with tender reach toward him.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、ばあさん、本気で、絶対、はやり、絶対、のお洋服、絶対、お召しになってたぞ、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: When you were young, Gran, you wore the loveliest fashionable clothes. I still remember. You do remember, don't you?
lines.style: Admiring, almost boyish in its appreciation. Steady, affectionate pace. A hint of amusement underneath — he's enjoying the picture of her he's seeing. Slight warmth on 「ぞ」 at the end.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、お祖父ちゃん、ご友人の名前、本気で、絶対、思い出せ、絶対、ない時、絶対、お困りだったわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Oh, your grandfather — he'd get so flustered when he couldn't remember his friends' names. Isn't that funny? Do you remember, dear?
lines.style: Gentle teasing affection mixed with fondness. Light, almost laughing tone but never unkind. Swift pace on the middle. Closes with warmth and knowing familiarity, like sharing a private joke.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、ばあさん、辛い時も、本気で、絶対、逃げ出し、絶対、ずに、絶対、頑張ってくれたぞ、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: When things were hard, Gran, you never gave up. You kept going with such strength. I've never forgotten that.
lines.style: Serious and grounded, with deep respect underneath. Slower pace, each phrase weighted. No performance — just honest acknowledgment. Slight tremor of emotion held steady in the voice.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、お祖父ちゃん、お父さんの、本気で、絶対、見落とし、絶対、ない、絶対、お仕事、絶対、立派でしたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: And your grandfather's work — the way he never missed a single detail with your father's business — it was truly fine. Such care. Don't you remember, dear?
lines.style: Firm with quiet pride. Steady, deliberate pacing that underscores the seriousness of the tribute. Warm but not soft — this is genuine admiration spoken plainly. Closes with a gentle reach for her agreement.
